Under § 4.1 Charges are only for Services ordered under Service Option Attachments and Order Forms (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), i.e. fees for usage or ordered services only, which matches our preferred position. § 11.5 Capacity Planning imposes no usage floor or cap on Customer — it merely allocates responsibility to Customer for sizing and requesting capacity changes. Customer also retains an exit under § 3.4, terminating the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for convenience at month end on one month's notice, subject only to early termination charges "if any" specified in Attachment A / Service Option Attachments (not part of this document). No redline required; we would review Attachment A and each Order Form for any committed volumes or early termination charges before signature.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant and the rendered redline is byte-identical to the originals with no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding. Cited text supports the preferred position: § 4.1 (p0052) ties Charges solely to Services specified in Service Option Attachments/Order Forms (one-time, installment, recurring or usage), with no minimum, committed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic. p0142 (Capacity Planning) allocates sizing responsibility to Customer but imposes no usage floor or volume cap, so it is correctly read as out of scope for MINCOMMIT. Exit right is corroborated: p0044/p0046 give Customer termination for convenience at month end, with early termination charges only 'if any' in Attachment A / Service Option Attachments; the rationale properly flags those documents (and Order Forms) for pre-signature review rather than overstating compliance. No deterministic check failures; nothing in the supplied paragraphs indicates a deviation requiring an actionable edit.

quote: Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.
rationale: Compliant with the preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"): the Base Terms impose no non-solicitation, no-hire or inducement restriction on Bluefly. § 14.8 Personnel deals only with each party's supervision of its own personnel, IBM's right to assign its personnel and IBM's right to subcontract; § 14.16 Freedom of Action goes the other way, confirming "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others." I also read the Preamble and definitions in full (pp0000-p0036) and ran full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "employ", "induce", "recruit" and "personnel"; the only "employ" hits are the Content Administrator definition and the indemnity clauses. No restrictive covenant exists. Accordingly no redline and no counterparty comment are proposed - inserting a 12-month cap or a general-solicitation carve-out would require first drafting in a restriction against ourselves, which is worse than the status quo. The failed sub-checks on duration and general-solicitation carve-out are therefore non-probative. Residual scope note: the Agreement also incorporates Order Forms, Attachment A (Facilities Services) and the Service Option Attachments, which are not part of the reviewed text; if any of those contains a hiring restriction we would negotiate to the fallback (mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and no no-hire).

verification.notes: general-solicitation carve-out present: failed Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: § 14.8 addresses only each party's supervision/assignment of its own personnel and IBM's subcontracting rights, and § 14.16 ('Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others.') is permissive rather than restrictive — none of the quoted paragraphs impose a non-solicit, no-hire or inducement restriction on the Customer. This matches the rule's preferred position ('No non-solicit on Customer'), so no redline and no counterparty comment are expected or appropriate; the rendered redline is correctly identical to the original. The failed deterministic sub-checks (duration ≤ 12 months, general-solicitation carve-out) are non-probative here because those elements only apply where a restrictive covenant exists; drafting a capped non-solicit into an agreement that has none would worsen the Customer's position. The rationale documents the search methodology and appropriately flags the residual scope limitation (Order Forms, Attachment A, Service Option Attachments not reviewed) with the fallback position to apply if a hiring restriction appears there — retained as internal evidence, not a negotiation issue.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We shortened the non-renewal notice window from 90 to 30 days, fixed renewal terms at twelve months, and capped any renewal price increase at the lesser of CPI and 3%, consistent with our position that renewals be easy to exit and predictably priced. If helpful, we can accept a 60-day window with a 5% uplift cap as a fallback.

ops.newText: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term of twelve (12) months unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment. IBM will notify Customer in writing of the upcoming renewal and the Charges applicable to the renewal term at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. Charges for any renewal term will not increase by more than the lesser of (i) the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%) over the Charges for the then-current term.
ops.oldText: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.

proposal.summary: Limit auto-renewal to 12 months, shorten Customer's non-renewal notice to 30 days with a 60-day IBM reminder, and cap renewal price increases.

quote: Each Service Option Attachment will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term
rationale: § 3.2 auto-renews each Service Option Attachment for a term equal to the prior term (which, where an Order Form specifies a multi-year initial term, produces automatic multi-year renewals at the walk-away boundary) and requires a 90-day non-renewal notice, exceeding both the preferred 30-day and fallback 60-day windows. Neither § 3.2 nor § 4.1 (Charges) constrains renewal pricing, leaving uplift uncapped. Redline fixes renewal terms at 12 months, shortens Customer's opt-out to 30 days, adds a 60-day IBM renewal reminder, and caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

checks.detail: changed-character ratio=0.663 (advisory: whole-clause rewrites are acceptable when the rule requires them)
checks.name: minimal edit p0040

verification.notes: Finding is directionally correct: original § 3.2 imposes a 90-day non-renewal notice window (worse than both the 30-day preferred and 60-day fallback) and renews for a term equal to the prior term, which permits automatic multi-year renewals at the walk-away boundary, with no cap on renewal pricing. Redline reaches the preferred position on each element: renewal term fixed at twelve (12) months, notice window shortened to thirty (30) days, a 60-day vendor renewal/pricing reminder added, and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Failed deterministic check 'non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days (number not found)' is a phrasing artifact — the redline plainly states 'at least thirty (30) days prior' — and the 0.663 changed-character ratio is justified because the rule requires inserting a reminder obligation and an uplift cap that have no counterpart in the original sentence. Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains the change and rationale, and offers the 60-day / 5% fallback. Note for negotiation (not a defect): the notice provision remains mutual, so shortening it to 30 days also lets IBM exit on 30 days' notice; if continuity matters, consider making the 30-day right Customer-only while leaving IBM at 90 days.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that a convenience exit must be penalty-free with a pro-rata refund of prepaid charges, so we removed the open-ended early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A and added the refund. If a charge is essential, we can accept a cap of three months' charges for the terminated Services as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Remove uncapped early termination charges from Customer's convenience right and add pro-rata refund of prepaid charges.

quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
rationale: Section 3.4 does give Customer a convenience right on roughly 30 days' notice (one month's notice, effective at month end), and IBM has no convenience right anywhere in the Agreement (3.3 is for-cause only), which matches our preferred position. However, the right is conditioned on paying open-ended early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, and there is no refund of prepaid charges (3.5 only accelerates Customer's payment obligations). That makes the exit penalty-bearing and uncapped, short of the preferred "without penalty plus pro-rata refund" position. Redline deletes the uncapped charge and adds a 30-day pro-rata refund, with a 3-months'-charges cap offered as fallback.

verification.notes: Deviation classification is correct on the substance: Section 3.4 gives Customer a convenience right (~one month's notice) and IBM has no convenience right, but subsection (b) conditions exit on open-ended early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, with no pro-rata refund — short of the preferred penalty-free exit with refund. Redline is targeted and actionable: it replaces only the offending payment condition in p0046 with (i) payment of charges accrued through the termination date, (ii) an express bar on early termination charges/penalties, and (iii) a 30-day pro-rata refund of prepaid charges. It correctly leaves the existing notice mechanics in p0044–p0045 alone rather than duplicating a convenience right. Failed deterministic checks are explained by the fact pattern, not by a defect: the 'Customer convenience termination present' regex misses because the right already exists in p0044 (no need to insert model language), and the 0.824 changed-character ratio reflects the fact that the whole point of the edit is to substitute the early-termination-charge obligation, which cannot be achieved with a smaller edit. Comment is accurate, in-voice, cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback (3 months' charges cap) consistent with the rule's fallback tier. Minor, non-blocking gap: the redline does not address the 'end of any calendar month' timing restriction in p0044, which can push an exit slightly beyond 30 days; worth flagging in the comment but it does not undermine the edit.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added an orderly exit right: up to six months of transition assistance at IBM's then-current rates, return of our Content in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter, since the Effect of Termination section is currently silent on data return. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance with the same thirty-day export window.

ops.text: Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason, IBM shall: (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months following the effective date of termination, at IBM's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return to Customer, or make available for retrieval by Customer, all Content in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all Content remaining in IBM's systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and Content return/deletion obligations into Section 3.5 (Effect of Termination).

quote: Upon the date of termination, all Customer payment obligations accrued hereunder through the date of termination will become due and payable. The termination of selected Service Option Attachments will not affect Customer's obligation to pay charges under other Service Option Attachments.
rationale: Section 3.5 (Effect of Termination) addresses only Customer's payment obligations; the Agreement contains no transition assistance, Content return/export, or deletion-certification obligation anywhere (searches for "transition", "delete" and "return" surface nothing relevant, and 14.18 Data Protection is limited to contact information). In a hosting agreement where all Customer data resides in IBM's e-business Hosting Environment, this leaves us with no exit path for our Content. We inserted the playbook transition clause into 3.5, which already survives termination under 14.2, so no survival amendment is needed.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

verification.notes: Missing-clause claim is supported: p0049 (Effect of Termination) addresses only payment obligations, and no transition assistance, data return/export, or deletion-certification obligation appears in the cited text. Redline is a pure insertion into the termination section with no alteration of existing language — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position, and it tracks the model language closely (6 months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion thereafter). Party and defined-term adaptation is correct (IBM as Vendor, 'Content' as the customer-data term, extension to Service Option Attachments), and survival is already secured because Section 3.5 is enumerated in the survival clause at p0169, so no additional amendment is needed. Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position, and offers the 90-day fallback with the same 30-day export window; deterministic checks confirm the operation applied and the transition/data-return language is present. Minor, non-blocking drafting nuance: clause (b) conditions the 30-day return on 'Customer's request', slightly narrower than the unconditional model language, but this remains actionable and within the preferred position.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5.1 gives us a services standard but no warranty that Materials conform to their documentation, no malicious code warranty and no remedy, and § 5.4(c) puts all Materials "AS IS", which swallows the express warranty. We added a 90-day conformance and malicious code warranty with re-performance, repair, replacement or refund, and carved the § 5.1 warranties out of the disclaimer; we can discuss a shorter conformance period if needed.

Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 5.1 is, at IBM's option, re-performance of the non-conforming Services, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Materials, or a refund of the charges paid for the non-conforming Services or Materials.

ops.newText: c. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1, IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES
ops.oldText: c. IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES

proposal.summary: Add deliverable conformance warranty, no-malicious-code warranty and a repair/replace/refund remedy to § 5.1, and carve the express warranties out of the § 5.4(c) "AS IS" disclaimer.

quote: c. IBM PROVIDES ALL MATERIALS AND ALL NON-IBM SERVICES, PRODUCTS, DATA, APPARATUS AND SOFTWARE "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, SATISFACTORY QUALITY, AND FITNESS FOR&sbsp;A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
rationale: § 5.1 contains only a "reasonable care and skill" services standard (broadly equivalent to professional and workmanlike) plus authority and a narrow law-compliance covenant. There is no warranty that Materials/deliverables conform to documentation, no malicious code warranty, and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy anywhere in the agreement (searches for "conform", "malicious" and "remedy" return nothing relevant). Worse, § 5.4(c) provides all Materials "AS IS" with no carve-out, so the disclaimer swallows any deliverable-level protection — close to the walk-away position. Redline adds a 90-day conformance warranty, a malicious code warranty and an at-IBM's-option re-performance/repair/replacement/refund remedy, and carves the § 5.1 warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision, so we added our standard coverage requirements (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, and cyber USD 5M since IBM hosts and processes Customer Data and personal data on our behalf under §§ 5.3 and 14.18), plus certificates on request. ops.text: IBM shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results and the section outline contains no insurance provision, so the Agreement is silent on vendor coverage.
